rows.grounds: demonstrative pronoun referring to a fruit/result
relative pronoun introducing the compared attainment
first member of compound qualifying thousand names
second member of compound qualifying names
final member of compound denoting the thousand names of Gaṇeśa
instrument denoting the act of recollection

items.question: What fruit remains unattained that remembrance of Gaṇeśa’s thousand names does not immediately grant?
premises: Remembrance of Gaṇeśa’s thousand names produces a fruit immediately.
The verse negates the existence of any fruit not obtained through this remembrance.
Therefore the practice is presented as universally efficacious for attaining desired results.
items.inference: There is no fruit that is not immediately obtained by remembering the thousand names of Gaṇeśa.
uncertainties: The exact syntactic scope of the negation with the relative clause is compressed and allows slight interpretive variation.
items.plain_english: There is no fruit that one fails to obtain immediately by remembering the thousand names of Gaṇeśa.
